question.text: Class <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>XII</mi></math> students were asked to prepare one litre of buffer solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi><mo> </mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>26</mn></math> by their chemistry teacher. The amount of ammonium chloride to be dissolved by the student in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> ammonia solution to make one litre of the buffer is (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>pK</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub><mfenced><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>74</mn><mo>;</mo></math> Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mi>Cl</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>53</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
A mixture of NH3 and NH4Cl will form a basic buffer.

pH of final solution =8.26

pOH of final solution=14-8.26 =5.74

Let the number of moles of NH4Cl added to 1 L solution of be x.

Using Henderson’s equation.

pOH=pKb+logNH4ClNH3

5.74=4.74+logx0.2

∴ x=2

The amount of ammonium chloride to be dissolved by the student in 0.2M ammonia solution to make one litre of buffer=2×53.5=107g
